Interface Provider<T>

Type Parameters:
T - The service interface created by this provider.
All Known Subinterfaces:
DocumentAnnotatorProvider, TextEmbedderProvider
public interface Provider<T>
Creates instances of one service interface from a ProviderSpec.

Every service interface has an SPI of its own that extends this interface, for example DocumentAnnotatorProvider extends Provider<DocumentAnnotator>. Implementations are listed in META-INF/services/<SPI fully qualified name>, need a public no-argument constructor and are resolved through Providers.

Implementations must be stateless and thread-safe. The constructor, the static initializer of the implementation class, isAvailable() and supports(ProviderSpec) must not load models or initialize native libraries: they run while providers are looked up, before a caller has chosen one.

Since:
3.0.0

  • Method Details

    • name

      String name()
      Returns:
      The case-sensitive name of this provider: at most 64 characters of ASCII letters, digits, ., _ or -, since it is used as a configuration value. A provider with another name is skipped when providers are looked up. Providers of one SPI may share a name; priority() ranks them.

    • priority

      default int priority()
      Returns:
      The rank of this provider among providers that support the same spec, larger wins. The default is 0.

    • isAvailable

      default boolean isAvailable()
      Checks whether this provider can be used in the running process, for example whether an optional dependency is on the class path. Check a class by class literal and catch LinkageError instead of loading it by name, which also keeps a native image free of reflection metadata. The check runs on every resolution, so it must not block.
      Returns:
      true if this provider can be used. The default is true.

    • supports

      boolean supports(ProviderSpec spec)
      Checks whether this provider can create an instance for a spec, based on the spec alone. The check runs on every resolution, so it must not block.
      Parameters:
      spec - The spec to check. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      true if create(ProviderSpec) accepts spec.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if spec is null.

    • create

      T create(ProviderSpec spec) throws IOException
      Creates a new instance. The caller owns it and closes it if it is closeable. The location of the spec is unvalidated input of the caller: a provider that opens it decides itself which schemes and which directories it accepts.
      Parameters:
      spec - The spec to create an instance for. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      The new instance. Never null.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if spec is null or not supported.
      IOException - Thrown if a resource named by spec could not be read.
